newsitem.title: UK: Gasoline set to improve in Med, fuel oil slips.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline set to improve in Med, fuel oil slips.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday with gasoline looking healthier, gas oil neutral and fuel oils slipping on the back of a cargo trade.

Gasoline prices held steady with supply fairly tight and demand expected to pick-up. Refinery turnarounds have tightened supplies and traders expected improving margins to encourage refiners to maximise on gasoline production.
Last week Mediterranean margins hit their highest level since last May. Complex margins averaged $3.47 a barrel last week, compared to an average of under $1 in January.

Traders said most people were covered until the middle of April because of turnarounds, but they expected both local and arbitrage buying to pick up soon. Naphtha held steady at lower levels, mainly on firmer crude, in an otherwise quiet market.
Gas oil was balanced, if fairly thin, with the only active discussion centred on sales of Russian cargoes into Lebanon.
Russian was talked around fob high quotes +$11-$12 a tonne for delivery into Lebanon, roughly equal to quotes high +$3-$3.50 cif Genoa, but traders said this market was not talked.
The Italian fob heating oil market was also thin with scarce barrels matched by nonchalant buying interest.

High sulphur fuel values dipped after Spanish refiner Repsol sold a cargo of bunker spec cracked fuel from Cartagena to an Italian trader on Friday for $79 fob, much lower than numbers talked by the regional market last week in pricing ploys.
"High sulphur has been overpriced for the last 15 days because it was in the interests of certain players to keep it so," said one Med fuel oil trader.
While some said the Repsol number was below the market, others pointed to healthier supply than of late and weak demand.
Low sulphur markets were again dead quiet and Russian straight-run cargoes overhung the market.
